bibl.title: Hybrid Offspring of C57BL/6J Mice Exhibit Improved Properties for Neurobehavioral Research

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether first-generation offspring of two inbred strains are a preferable model for neurobehavioral studies
span.quote: We bred FVB/NJ females and C57BL/6J males to generate first-generation hybrid offspring (FVB/NJ x C57BL/6J)F1. The hybrid mice exhibit reduced anxiety-like behavior, improved learning, and enhanced long-term spatial memory. In contrast to both progenitors, hybrids maintain sensorimotor performance upon aging and exhibit improved long-term memory.

span.label: how to balance convenient genetic control against the complex behavior that inbred strains cannot support
span.quote: Because of genetic tools, mice are increasingly used for neuroscience experiments that were traditionally performed using rats. However, mice are smaller and “less intelligent” than rats, limiting the size of neural implants and the complexity of performed behaviors. Here, we show that these problems are exacerbated by the widespread use of inbred C57BL/6J mice, which are small animals with behavioral and sensorimotor deficits that worsen with age. In line with the established principle of hybrid vigor, we found that first-generation offspring of C57BL/6J and FVB/NJ mice exhibit improved learning and memory, maintain sensorimotor performance on aging, are larger, and exhibit improved behavior while carrying a chronic implant. The hybrid mice allow genetic control while supporting complex behavior over prolonged durations.

span.label: a single well-defined outbreeding step produces larger offspring that exhibit enhanced behavior even during electrophysiology experiments, maintaining the ability of genetic targeting
span.quote: A single well-defined outbreeding step produces larger offspring that exhibit enhanced behavior even during electrophysiology experiments, maintaining the ability of genetic targeting.

span.label: method
span.quote: The hybrid mice provide an improved model for neurobehavioral studies combining complex behavior, electrophysiology, and genetic tools readily available in C57BL/6 mice.

span.label: hybrid vigour in laboratory mouse phenotype
span.quote: In line with the established principle of hybrid vigor, we found that first-generation offspring of C57BL/6J and FVB/NJ mice exhibit improved learning and memory, maintain sensorimotor performance on aging, are larger, and exhibit improved behavior while carrying a chronic implant.

span.label: behavioral-experiment
span.quote: Animals assigned to Battery A were subjected to assays in the following order: elevated plus maze (1 d); open field (1 d); rotarod (5 d); treadmill (3 d); optomotor drum (1 d); and forced swim test (1 d).

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: In line with the established principle of hybrid vigor, we found that first-generation offspring of C57BL/6J and FVB/NJ mice exhibit improved learning and memory, maintain sensorimotor performance on aging, are larger, and exhibit improved behavior while carrying a chronic implant.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: However, inbreeding exposes undesired phenotypical traits because of homozygous recessive alleles and does not guarantee stability over generations because of genetic drift ( Brekke et al., 2018 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: HYB impaired balance may result from weight differences between the strains since HYB weigh more, and weight affects rotarod performance ( Mao et al., 2015 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: The difference between brain regions is consistent with different network topologies, since in contrast to the neocortex, CA1 PYR do not exhibit abundant recurrent excitation ( Thomson and Radpour, 1991 ; Buhl and Whittington, 2007 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: Since headgear weight is limited by body size, the range of studied behaviors is limited by animal weight.

span.label: inbreeding EXPOSES UNDESIRED PHENOTYPICAL TRAITS because of homozygous recessive alleles, and DOES NOT GUARANTEE STABILITY OVER GENERATIONS because of genetic drift
span.quote: However, inbreeding exposes undesired phenotypical traits because of homozygous recessive alleles and does not guarantee stability over generations because of genetic drift ( Brekke et al., 2018 ).

span.label: and the hybrid inherits one allele from each parent, so the recessive traits are not expressed - 25% of the F2 generation would be blind because of a functional copy of the Pde6b gene MAINTAINED IN EVERY F1 HYBRID
span.quote: We focused on first generation (F1) hybrids to minimize genetic differences between individuals. While further breeding is expected to increase intersubject genetic variability, F2 hybrids will necessarily express recessive traits not expressed by the F1 generation. For instance, 25% of the F2 hybrids are expected to be blind because of a functional copy of the Pde6b gene ( Pittler and Baehr, 1991 ) maintained in every F1 hybrid. Thus, unless careful backcrossing is performed, F2 hybrids should not be used.

span.label: SINCE HEADGEAR WEIGHT IS LIMITED BY BODY SIZE, THE RANGE OF STUDIED BEHAVIORS IS LIMITED BY ANIMAL WEIGHT - and the hybrids are heavier than either progenitor
span.quote: C57 mice are also smaller than other strains, which is a disadvantage for electrophysiological studies involving implanted headgear. Since headgear weight is limited by body size, the range of studied behaviors is limited by animal weight.

span.label: Hybrids showed impaired balance at three months, so they may be unsuitable for balance studies.
span.quote: Although HYB balance performance improved upon aging, hybrids may be unsuitable for studies involving balance.

span.label: The hybrids' reduced and age-changing anxiety-like behavior makes them a poor model for long-term anxiety research.
span.quote: For instance, the overall reduced anxiety-like behavior and the age-related changes make the HYB less suitable for long-term studies of anxiety.

span.label: Only one cross direction (FVB dam x C57 sire) was characterized; the reciprocal cross was not tested.
span.quote: Full characterization is required before the use of reciprocal hybrids, offspring of a C57 female and an FVB male.

span.label: Hybrids are awkward for designs requiring homozygosity or double knock-out.
span.quote: Fourth, it is not straightforward to use hybrids if a homozygous allele is required or if knock-out of both copies of a given gene is required (although see Silva et al., 1997 ).

span.label: compared with the C57 progenitors, HYB exhibited similar or improved performance in every assay used, WITH ONE EXCEPTION: BALANCE PERFORMANCE in the three-month-old age group, so HYBRIDS MAY BE UNSUITABLE FOR STUDIES INVOLVING BALANCE
span.quote: There are some situations in which hybrid mice are not advantageous. First, compared with the C57 progenitors, HYB exhibited similar or improved performance in every assay used, with one exception: balance performance in the three-month-old age group. HYB impaired balance may result from weight differences between the strains since HYB weigh more, and weight affects rotarod performance ( Mao et al., 2015 ). Although HYB balance performance improved upon aging, hybrids may be unsuitable for studies involving balance.

span.label: REDUCED ANXIETY-LIKE BEHAVIOR MAY BE SUBOPTIMAL FOR OTHER PURPOSES - the overall reduced anxiety and the age-related changes make the HYB LESS SUITABLE FOR LONG-TERM STUDIES OF ANXIETY
span.quote: Second, while the reduced anxiety exhibited by HYB is beneficial for studies involving cognitive and motor tasks, reduced anxiety-like behavior may be suboptimal for other purposes. For instance, the overall reduced anxiety-like behavior and the age-related changes make the HYB less suitable for long-term studies of anxiety.

span.label: BECAUSE HYB MICE ARE MORE ROBUST, GENETIC KNOCK-OUT MANIPULATIONS MAY BE LESS LIKELY TO SHOW A CONSISTENT PHENOTYPIC CHANGE, and it is not straightforward to use hybrids if a homozygous allele is required
span.quote: Third, because HYB mice are more robust, genetic knock-out manipulations may be less likely to show a consistent phenotypic change ( Sittig et al., 2016 ). Fourth, it is not straightforward to use hybrids if a homozygous allele is required or if knock-out of both copies of a given gene is required (although see Silva et al., 1997 ).

span.label: some genes expressed by progenitors may be DOMINANT - FVB contain a Disc1 mutation shown to CAUSE COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT EVEN WHEN HETEROZYGOUS
span.quote: Third, some genes expressed by progenitors may be dominant; for instance, FVB contain a Disc1 mutation which has been shown to cause cognitive impairment even when heterozygous ( Koike et al., 2006 ; Ritchie and Clapcote, 2013 ). Nevertheless, we found that the potentially deleterious effects of dominant genes on HYB are smaller than the adverse effects of inbreeding.

span.label: FULL CHARACTERIZATION IS REQUIRED BEFORE THE USE OF RECIPROCAL HYBRIDS, and since interstrain differences are also sex-dependent, FEMALE HYB MAY EXHIBIT DISTINCT PHENOTYPES
span.quote: Second, we employed HYB which are offspring of FVB females and C57 males. Full characterization is required before the use of reciprocal hybrids, offspring of a C57 female and an FVB male. However, because of the reduced litter sizes of female C57 compared with female FVB ( Taketo et al., 1991 ; Silver, 1995 ), the usage of the reciprocal hybrids is not recommended. Finally, since interstrain differences are also sex-dependent ( Brown and Wong, 2007 ), female HYB may exhibit distinct phenotypes.

span.label: UNLESS CAREFUL BACKCROSSING IS PERFORMED, F2 HYBRIDS SHOULD NOT BE USED
span.quote: We focused on first generation (F1) hybrids to minimize genetic differences between individuals. While further breeding is expected to increase intersubject genetic variability, F2 hybrids will necessarily express recessive traits not expressed by the F1 generation. For instance, 25% of the F2 hybrids are expected to be blind because of a functional copy of the Pde6b gene ( Pittler and Baehr, 1991 ) maintained in every F1 hybrid. Thus, unless careful backcrossing is performed, F2 hybrids should not be used.

span.label: hybrid vigor, applied so that the first-generation offspring keep one transgenic allele from the C57 parent while losing the recessive traits of both
span.quote: Because of genetic tools, mice are increasingly used for neuroscience experiments that were traditionally performed using rats. However, mice are smaller and “less intelligent” than rats, limiting the size of neural implants and the complexity of performed behaviors. Here, we show that these problems are exacerbated by the widespread use of inbred C57BL/6J mice, which are small animals with behavioral and sensorimotor deficits that worsen with age. In line with the established principle of hybrid vigor, we found that first-generation offspring of C57BL/6J and FVB/NJ mice exhibit improved learning and memory, maintain sensorimotor performance on aging, are larger, and exhibit improved behavior while carrying a chronic implant. The hybrid mice allow genetic control while supporting complex behavior over prolonged durations.

span.label: the comparison with rats, where MICE ARE SMALLER AND LESS INTELLIGENT, LIMITING THE SIZE OF NEURAL IMPLANTS AND THE COMPLEXITY OF PERFORMED BEHAVIORS
span.quote: Because of genetic tools, mice are increasingly used for neuroscience experiments that were traditionally performed using rats. However, mice are smaller and “less intelligent” than rats, limiting the size of neural implants and the complexity of performed behaviors. Here, we show that these problems are exacerbated by the widespread use of inbred C57BL/6J mice, which are small animals with behavioral and sensorimotor deficits that worsen with age. In line with the established principle of hybrid vigor, we found that first-generation offspring of C57BL/6J and FVB/NJ mice exhibit improved learning and memory, maintain sensorimotor performance on aging, are larger, and exhibit improved behavior while carrying a chronic implant. The hybrid mice allow genetic control while supporting complex behavior over prolonged durations.

span.label: the 3Rs argument, derived here from the behavioral result rather than asserted separately
span.quote: The hybrid vigor and the enhanced behavioral capabilities may yield more trials in every experimental session, shorter learning periods, and higher accuracy in complex tasks. By increasing yield and accuracy, the usage of HYB may allow uncovering unexplored neuronal mechanisms. Enhanced behavior also has ethical advantages, since faster learning and higher yield per animal translate to fewer experimental animals or sessions required to answer a given question.

span.label: the same three strains tested at two ages rather than one
span.quote: Compared with the parental C57BL/6J progenitor strain, young first-generation hybrid offspring (FVB/NJ x C57BL/6J)F1 exhibited reduced anxiety-like behavior. Upon aging, HYB anxiety-like behavior was further reduced, and learning and long-term memory performance improved. In contrast, learning and memory performance of the parental C57BL/6J and the maternal FVB/NJ progenitor strains did not improve at older age. Furthermore, motor performance of the progenitor strains deteriorated upon aging, whereas HYB sensorimotor abilities were maintained. HYB were larger, ran faster, and performed more trials during electrophysiological experiments on the linear track. HYB and C57 exhibited similar CA1 place cell rate and phase coding. Finally, optogenetic manipulations were readily achieved in transgenic HYB.

span.label: an optomotor drum test of visual behavior run before the cognitive assays
span.quote: In contrast, FVB did not make any head turns (0 [0 0]; C57 vs FVB: p = 0.0011; HYB vs FVB: p = 0.003), consistent with blindness because of retinal degeneration ( Pittler and Baehr, 1991 ).

span.label: gait analysis and home cage behavior added to the standard battery
span.quote: Together, the weight, daily conduct, and gait differences indicate that the spontaneous behavior of the (FVB/NJ x C57BL/6J)F1 hybrids is distinct from that of both progenitor strains.

span.label: long-term memory scored two different ways on the same task
span.quote: Spatial long-term memory behavior on the MWM. a , When performance is quantified by the fraction of time spent in the target quadrant, there is no consistent difference between the strains. b , When performance is quantified by the fraction of visits to the target quadrant, HYB exhibit improved performance compared with C57 and to FVB.

span.label: THE PEER REVIEW IS PUBLISHED WITH THE PAPER, AND IT SAYS THE HEADLINE IS MISLEADING: MY MAIN CRITIC IS THAT THE MANUSCRIPT IS SOMEWHAT MISLEADING REGARDING THE NATURE OF THE DIFFERENCES - the overall impression from TITLE, ABSTRACT AND MAIN TEXT is that hybrids outperform regardless of age, but THERE IS NOT MUCH DIFFERENCE between hybrid and C57 for the 3-month old mice, and HYBRIDS PRESENT NO MAJOR ADVANTAGE WHEN YOUNG ADULT MICE ARE USED
span.quote: My main critic is that the manuscript is somewhat misleading regarding the nature of the differences between species. The major claim is that hybrids outperform both progenitor strains in several learning and motor tasks, and, in addition, show less aging-related deficits. The overall impression from title, abstract and main text is that hybrids outperform progenitor strains regardless of age. However, according to the data (supplementary figures 2 and 3), there is not much difference between hybrid and C57 strains for the 3-month old mice. The differences are mostly significant for 9-month old mice. Hence, hybrid and C57 mice start at the same level during early adulthood (3-months) and then C57 mice show reduced properties as they degrade faster with age. I think the manuscript should be clearer regarding that the effect of aging is explaining the better properties of hybrids at relatively old age (9-months) and that hybrids present no major advantage when young adult mice are used (except for their larger size).

span.label: and the editor makes it a condition rather than a suggestion: PLEASE REVISE THE MANUSCRIPT IN RESPONSE TO THESE COMMENTS. ADDRESSING THESE POINTS IS KEY FOR YOUR RESUBMISSION
span.quote: EDITOR COMMENT: Please revise the manuscript in response to these comments. Addressing these points is key for your resubmission.

span.label: A REVIEWER QUESTIONING A NUMBER, IN THE PUBLISHED RECORD: THE LED POWER USED IN OPTOGENETIC STUDY WAS 11.07 uW, WHICH SEEMS VERY LOW. IS THE UNIT USED HEREIN IS CORRECT? - and the editor: PLEASE CONFIRM OR REVISE THE LEVEL OF LIGHT USED
span.quote: The LED power used in optogenetic study was 11.07 μW, which seems very low. Is the unit used herein is correct? EDITOR COMMENT: Please confirm or revise the level of light used in the opto part of the study.

span.label: and a reviewer asking why the statistics are what they are: they need to EXPLICITLY MENTION IN METHODS WHY THEY USED NON-PARAMETRIC TEST, with the editor adding REPORT RESULTS FROM EXPLORATORY DATA ANALYSIS TO JUSTIFY USE OF NON-PARAMETRICS
span.quote: Authors used Kruskal Wallis test for several group's analysis. They need to explicitly mention in methods that why they used Non-parametric test. EDITOR COMMENT: Please clarify why non-parametric tests were used in the Methods section. Report results from exploratory data analysis to justify use of non-parametrics or state another reason.

span.label: with an editor's note that the vocabulary itself is not readable: PLEASE REVIEW TERMS USED FOR STATISTICAL TESTS THROUGHOUT THE PAPER. IT MIGHT NOT BE CLEAR TO MANY READERS WHAT YOU MEAN BY, E.G., U AND G TESTS
span.quote: EDITOR COMMENT: Please review terms used for statistical tests throughout the paper. It might not be clear to many readers what you mean by, e.g., U and G tests.

span.label: and the same document carries the opposite verdict, signed: THIS STUDY IS WELL DESIGNED, NICELY CONDUCTED AND EXCELLENTLY WRITTEN
span.quote: This study is well designed, nicely conducted and excellently written. I believe that this manuscript will be worth publishing in eNeuro following minor revision as suggested below.

span.label: with the reviewing editor named - MARK LAUBACH, AMERICAN UNIVERSITY - and one reviewer revealing his identity, SEBASTIEN ROYER
span.quote: Synthesis Reviewing Editor: Mark Laubach, American University Decisions are customarily a result of the Reviewing Editor and the peer reviewers coming together and discussing their recommendations until a consensus is reached. When revisions are invited, a fact-based synthesis statement explaining their decision and outlining what is needed to prepare a revision will be listed below. The following reviewer(s) agreed to reveal their identity: Sebastien Royer.

span.label: TWO WAYS OF SCORING ONE TASK GIVE OPPOSITE ANSWERS: when performance is quantified by the FRACTION OF TIME SPENT in the target quadrant, THERE IS NO CONSISTENT DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE STRAINS - when it is quantified by the FRACTION OF VISITS to the same quadrant, HYB EXHIBIT IMPROVED PERFORMANCE. Same animals, same trials, same figure
span.quote: Spatial long-term memory behavior on the MWM. a , When performance is quantified by the fraction of time spent in the target quadrant, there is no consistent difference between the strains. b , When performance is quantified by the fraction of visits to the target quadrant, HYB exhibit improved performance compared with C57 and to FVB.

span.label: THE MODEL DECIDES WHAT CAN BE STUDIED: SINCE HEADGEAR WEIGHT IS LIMITED BY BODY SIZE, THE RANGE OF STUDIED BEHAVIORS IS LIMITED BY ANIMAL WEIGHT
span.quote: C57 mice are also smaller than other strains, which is a disadvantage for electrophysiological studies involving implanted headgear. Since headgear weight is limited by body size, the range of studied behaviors is limited by animal weight.

span.label: and the same point about the strain's deficits: C57BL/6-derived mice exhibit sensitivity to pain, addiction, impaired balance, age-dependent hearing loss and increased anxiety - THUS, THE BEHAVIORAL TASKS STUDIED USING C57BL/6 ARE LIMITED
span.quote: C57BL/6-derived mice exhibit known phenotypic disadvantages, including sensitivity to pain, addiction, impaired balance, age-dependent hearing loss, and increased anxiety ( Crawley, 1996 ; Mogil et al., 1999 ; Ouagazzal et al., 2006 ). Thus, the behavioral tasks studied using C57BL/6 are limited.

span.label: STRAIN SELECTION CAN POTENTIALLY AFFECT RESEARCH OUTCOME, since strain characteristics MAY INTERACT WITH GENETIC MANIPULATIONS and with experimental ones - mice with retinal degeneration CANNOT FULLY USE VISUAL INFORMATION and are impaired on navigation tasks that rely on visual cues
span.quote: One of the challenges in mouse-based research is adjusting the strain to the specific study question. Strain selection can potentially affect research outcome, since strain characteristics may interact with genetic manipulations ( Sittig et al., 2016 ). Furthermore, strain characteristics could interact with experimental manipulations. For example, mice that suffer from retinal degeneration cannot fully use visual information and exhibit impaired behavior in hippocampal-based navigation tasks that rely on visual cues

span.label: and the control group is named as a thing that can drift: A SECOND CHALLENGE IS TO ENSURE THE STABILITY OF THE TESTED PHENOTYPE UNDER THE NULL CONDITION - DETERIORATION OF CONTROL PHENOTYPIC BEHAVIOR COULD CONFOUND potential manipulation-based intergroup differences
span.quote: A second challenge is to ensure the stability of the tested phenotype under the null condition throughout the study period. In many cases, the effects of a given manipulation are studied over weeks to months ( Prevot et al., 2019 ; Namdar et al., 2020 ; Rahn et al., 2021 ). Deterioration of control phenotypic behavior could confound potential manipulation-based intergroup differences.

span.label: with inbreeding's own instability stated: it EXPOSES UNDESIRED PHENOTYPICAL TRAITS because of homozygous recessive alleles and DOES NOT GUARANTEE STABILITY OVER GENERATIONS BECAUSE OF GENETIC DRIFT
span.quote: However, inbreeding exposes undesired phenotypical traits because of homozygous recessive alleles and does not guarantee stability over generations because of genetic drift ( Brekke et al., 2018 ).

span.label: A STRAIN THAT CANNOT SEE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: FVB DID NOT MAKE ANY HEAD TURNS, CONSISTENT WITH BLINDNESS BECAUSE OF RETINAL DEGENERATION - one of the two progenitors of the proposed model is blind
span.quote: In contrast, FVB did not make any head turns (0 [0 0]; C57 vs FVB: p = 0.0011; HYB vs FVB: p = 0.003), consistent with blindness because of retinal degeneration ( Pittler and Baehr, 1991 ).

span.label: and the recessive trait is carried invisibly by the hybrid: 25% OF THE F2 HYBRIDS ARE EXPECTED TO BE BLIND because of a functional copy of the Pde6b gene MAINTAINED IN EVERY F1 HYBRID - so UNLESS CAREFUL BACKCROSSING IS PERFORMED, F2 HYBRIDS SHOULD NOT BE USED
span.quote: We focused on first generation (F1) hybrids to minimize genetic differences between individuals. While further breeding is expected to increase intersubject genetic variability, F2 hybrids will necessarily express recessive traits not expressed by the F1 generation. For instance, 25% of the F2 hybrids are expected to be blind because of a functional copy of the Pde6b gene ( Pittler and Baehr, 1991 ) maintained in every F1 hybrid. Thus, unless careful backcrossing is performed, F2 hybrids should not be used.

span.label: THE EXCEPTIONS ARE LISTED BY THE AUTHORS, EACH WITH THE USE IT DISQUALIFIES: similar or improved performance in every assay WITH ONE EXCEPTION, BALANCE at three months - so HYBRIDS MAY BE UNSUITABLE FOR STUDIES INVOLVING BALANCE
span.quote: There are some situations in which hybrid mice are not advantageous. First, compared with the C57 progenitors, HYB exhibited similar or improved performance in every assay used, with one exception: balance performance in the three-month-old age group. HYB impaired balance may result from weight differences between the strains since HYB weigh more, and weight affects rotarod performance ( Mao et al., 2015 ). Although HYB balance performance improved upon aging, hybrids may be unsuitable for studies involving balance.

span.label: and reduced anxiety cuts both ways - beneficial for cognitive and motor tasks, but the reduced anxiety and the age-related changes MAKE THE HYB LESS SUITABLE FOR LONG-TERM STUDIES OF ANXIETY
span.quote: Second, while the reduced anxiety exhibited by HYB is beneficial for studies involving cognitive and motor tasks, reduced anxiety-like behavior may be suboptimal for other purposes. For instance, the overall reduced anxiety-like behavior and the age-related changes make the HYB less suitable for long-term studies of anxiety.

span.label: AND THE MODEL'S OWN ROBUSTNESS IS NAMED AS A LIABILITY: BECAUSE HYB MICE ARE MORE ROBUST, GENETIC KNOCK-OUT MANIPULATIONS MAY BE LESS LIKELY TO SHOW A CONSISTENT PHENOTYPIC CHANGE - the healthier animal hides the effect being looked for
span.quote: Third, because HYB mice are more robust, genetic knock-out manipulations may be less likely to show a consistent phenotypic change ( Sittig et al., 2016 ). Fourth, it is not straightforward to use hybrids if a homozygous allele is required or if knock-out of both copies of a given gene is required (although see Silva et al., 1997 ).

span.label: with a dominant mutation carried by one progenitor: FVB CONTAIN A DISC1 MUTATION WHICH HAS BEEN SHOWN TO CAUSE COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT EVEN WHEN HETEROZYGOUS - and the paper weighs it against inbreeding rather than dismissing it
span.quote: Third, some genes expressed by progenitors may be dominant; for instance, FVB contain a Disc1 mutation which has been shown to cause cognitive impairment even when heterozygous ( Koike et al., 2006 ; Ritchie and Clapcote, 2013 ). Nevertheless, we found that the potentially deleterious effects of dominant genes on HYB are smaller than the adverse effects of inbreeding.

span.label: and two whole conditions left uncharacterized: FULL CHARACTERIZATION IS REQUIRED BEFORE THE USE OF RECIPROCAL HYBRIDS, and FEMALE HYB MAY EXHIBIT DISTINCT PHENOTYPES - every number in this paper is from male mice of one cross direction
span.quote: Second, we employed HYB which are offspring of FVB females and C57 males. Full characterization is required before the use of reciprocal hybrids, offspring of a C57 female and an FVB male. However, because of the reduced litter sizes of female C57 compared with female FVB ( Taketo et al., 1991 ; Silver, 1995 ), the usage of the reciprocal hybrids is not recommended. Finally, since interstrain differences are also sex-dependent ( Brown and Wong, 2007 ), female HYB may exhibit distinct phenotypes.

span.label: the size result stated with its purpose attached: HYB were LARGER THAN EITHER PARENTAL STRAIN, and HIGHER WEIGHTS ARE BENEFICIAL FOR ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL EXPERIMENTS in freely-moving animals, IN WHICH ANIMAL SIZE LIMITS THE WEIGHT OF THE IMPLANTED APPARATUS
span.quote: We found that sedentary HYB were larger than either parental strain. At the age of three months, the median [IQR] weight of HYB was 32 [29.6 34.9] g, compared with 26.9 [25.1 28.1] g for C57 ( p = 9.6 × 10 −10 ; Kruskal–Wallis test, corrected for multiple comparisons; Fig. 1 ; Extended Data Fig. 1-1 A ). Higher weights are beneficial for electrophysiological experiments in freely-moving animals, in which animal size limits the weight of the implanted apparatus.

span.label: and the one assay where the hybrids do worse, reported plainly: HYB LATENCY TO FALL DID NOT INCREASE OVER DAYS - no balance learning, where both progenitors showed it
span.quote: HYB latency to fall did not increase over days ( p = 0.12, Kruskal–Wallis test). To summarize, at the age of three months, visual behavior, and motor endurance of HYB are similar to those of C57.

span.label: with an ethical argument made from a behavioral one: faster learning and higher yield per animal TRANSLATE TO FEWER EXPERIMENTAL ANIMALS OR SESSIONS REQUIRED TO ANSWER A GIVEN QUESTION
span.quote: The hybrid vigor and the enhanced behavioral capabilities may yield more trials in every experimental session, shorter learning periods, and higher accuracy in complex tasks. By increasing yield and accuracy, the usage of HYB may allow uncovering unexplored neuronal mechanisms. Enhanced behavior also has ethical advantages, since faster learning and higher yield per animal translate to fewer experimental animals or sessions required to answer a given question.

span.label: builds-on → Blednov et al. (2005, 2010), on C57BL/6J x FVB/NJ offspring as an alcohol-consumption model
span.quote: Previous work has shown that offspring of C57BL/6J (C57) and FVB/NJ (FVB) mice consume more alcohol than either progenitor, serving as a preferable model for alcohol consumption ( Blednov et al., 2005 , 2010 ).

span.label: replicates → Stark et al. (2012), distance-dependent optogenetic activation in rat hippocampus
span.quote: As previously reported in rat hippocampus ( Stark et al., 2012 ), activation probability depended on the horizontal distance from the light source.

span.label: replicates → Stark et al. (2013), indirect interneuron activation in C57 mice
span.quote: Thus, consistent with previous observations in C57 mice ( Stark et al., 2013 ), indirect INT activation in CA1 leads to more widespread activation than the local activation achieved in PYR.

span.label: qualifies → its own headline, which the published review says reads as an advantage at any age when the difference is mostly in the older group
span.quote: My main critic is that the manuscript is somewhat misleading regarding the nature of the differences between species. The major claim is that hybrids outperform both progenitor strains in several learning and motor tasks, and, in addition, show less aging-related deficits. The overall impression from title, abstract and main text is that hybrids outperform progenitor strains regardless of age. However, according to the data (supplementary figures 2 and 3), there is not much difference between hybrid and C57 strains for the 3-month old mice. The differences are mostly significant for 9-month old mice. Hence, hybrid and C57 mice start at the same level during early adulthood (3-months) and then C57 mice show reduced properties as they degrade faster with age. I think the manuscript should be clearer regarding that the effect of aging is explaining the better properties of hybrids at relatively old age (9-months) and that hybrids present no major advantage when young adult mice are used (except for their larger size).

span.label: critiques → the widespread use of one inbred strain, whose deficits limit which behavioral tasks can be studied at all
span.quote: C57BL/6-derived mice exhibit known phenotypic disadvantages, including sensitivity to pain, addiction, impaired balance, age-dependent hearing loss, and increased anxiety ( Crawley, 1996 ; Mogil et al., 1999 ; Ouagazzal et al., 2006 ). Thus, the behavioral tasks studied using C57BL/6 are limited.

span.label: extends → the established principle of hybrid vigor, applied to the specific pairing that keeps C57-background transgenic tools usable
span.quote: Because of genetic tools, mice are increasingly used for neuroscience experiments that were traditionally performed using rats. However, mice are smaller and “less intelligent” than rats, limiting the size of neural implants and the complexity of performed behaviors. Here, we show that these problems are exacerbated by the widespread use of inbred C57BL/6J mice, which are small animals with behavioral and sensorimotor deficits that worsen with age. In line with the established principle of hybrid vigor, we found that first-generation offspring of C57BL/6J and FVB/NJ mice exhibit improved learning and memory, maintain sensorimotor performance on aging, are larger, and exhibit improved behavior while carrying a chronic implant. The hybrid mice allow genetic control while supporting complex behavior over prolonged durations.

span.label: supports → strain selection as a design decision that can affect research outcome, because strain characteristics interact with the manipulations under test
span.quote: One of the challenges in mouse-based research is adjusting the strain to the specific study question. Strain selection can potentially affect research outcome, since strain characteristics may interact with genetic manipulations ( Sittig et al., 2016 ). Furthermore, strain characteristics could interact with experimental manipulations. For example, mice that suffer from retinal degeneration cannot fully use visual information and exhibit impaired behavior in hippocampal-based navigation tasks that rely on visual cues

span.label: predicts → that female hybrids and the reciprocal cross may behave differently, and that both need full characterisation before use
span.quote: Second, we employed HYB which are offspring of FVB females and C57 males. Full characterization is required before the use of reciprocal hybrids, offspring of a C57 female and an FVB male. However, because of the reduced litter sizes of female C57 compared with female FVB ( Taketo et al., 1991 ; Silver, 1995 ), the usage of the reciprocal hybrids is not recommended. span.label: aging —causes→ C57
span.quote: My main critic is that the manuscript is somewhat misleading regarding the nature of the differences between species. The major claim is that hybrids outperform both progenitor strains in several learning and motor tasks, and, in addition, show less aging-related deficits. The overall impression from title, abstract and main text is that hybrids outperform progenitor strains regardless of age. However, according to the data (supplementary figures 2 and 3), there is not much difference between hybrid and C57 strains for the 3-month old mice. The differences are mostly significant for 9-month old mice. Hence, hybrid and C57 mice start at the same level during early adulthood (3-months) and then C57 mice show reduced properties as they degrade faster with age.
